## `73906110dd67`

The canonical setting orders objects by occupied area. The alternative orders by
bounding-box area, with occupied area as tie-breaker. Inputs contain a sparse 3x3
object whose bounding box outranks a denser 4x2 object, so the input-derived
intermediate order changes. The output packer consumes that order. Matched inputs,
2–6 prefix-stable demonstrations, four queries, and a 30x30 query are retained.

Evidence: `checks/73906110dd67-tests/result.json`,
`checks/73906110dd67/qualification/qualification.json`,
`checks/73906110dd67/causal/witness.json`, and
`checks/73906110dd67/first-turn.json`.

## `72b99d3a9be8`

The old sampler's claimed wall-orientation branch was not trustworthy: its normal
shape was horizontal-only, and extra color-2 bars could bounce the ray before the
sampled wall. The repair constructs real horizontal/vertical reflectors, keeps
color 2 unique to the intended reflector, uses color 3 for pass-through decoys,
and validates strict overrides. The parametric alternative makes color 3 the
reflector. Both colors occur on matched inputs with opposing wall orientations,
so the bounce-event intermediate and final path differ. The canonical rule text
and authority remain unchanged.

Evidence: `checks/72b99d3a9be8-tests/result.json`,
`checks/72b99d3a9be8/qualification/qualification.json`,
`checks/72b99d3a9be8/causal/witness.json`, and
`checks/72b99d3a9be8/first-turn.json`.

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h, w~9-13) with ONE DIAGONAL PAIR of COLOR-1 cells: (a) DOWN-RIGHT pair: (r, c) and (r+1, c+1), or (b) DOWN-LEFT pair: (r, c+1) and (r+1, c). The pair is placed at interior position (r, c) with margins ≥3 from all sides (room for diagonal extension). Rule (DIAGONAL PAIR EXTENDS IN BOTH DIAGONAL DIRECTIONS, BOUNCING FROM COLOR-2 WALLS WHEN PRESENT): the pair defines a DIAGONAL DIRECTION (down-right or down-left). PROJECT the pair OUTWARD in BOTH diagonal directions (forward and backward), painting each diagonal cell COLOR 1, until either: (i) hitting a COLOR-2 WALL (the beam bounces — direction reverses or reflects per puzzle convention), or (ii) hitting the grid edge. Net: the diagonal pair extends into a full diagonal line spanning the grid.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The ordered bounce events: hit coordinates, measured wall orientations, phases, and incoming and outgoing beam directions.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Trace the diagonal seed until cells of the selected reflector color are hit, measuring each wall orientation and deriving the ordered bounce-event sequence.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Continue and paint the beam from each bounce using the outgoing direction derived from that event until the path exits or reaches another selected reflector.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The later painted path cannot be chosen before A identifies the selected-color wall and its orientation; substituting the other color's events changes the trajectory and final grid.
